issues.legal_issue: The additional acquisition amount is not available merely because a reference court decides the compensation claim after an amendment takes effect when the acquisition and the collector’s award predate the amendment’s transitional trigger.
material_facts: The acquisition proceedings began before the transitional trigger and the Collector made the award before that trigger.
The claimants sought a reference, and the Civil Court enhanced compensation after the amendment had taken effect.

The acquisition did not fall within either of the amendment’s specified transitional categories: an acquisition pending at the trigger with no Collector’s award yet made, or an acquisition commenced after the trigger.
issues.conclusion: The Court considered the claimants not entitled to the additional amount on these facts. It held that the contrary interpretation in Zora Singh conferred a benefit beyond the amendment’s limited transitional provisions and required reconsideration, so it referred the matter to a larger Bench rather than finally resolving the conflict.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1-A) forms part of the substantive scheme for determining compensation, read with Sections 11 and 15 and the governing market-value date under Section 23(1). A substantive amendment operates prospectively unless retrospective effect is provided expressly or by necessary intendment. Section 30(1)(a) and (b) supplies limited retrospective operation for its specified transitional categories; the Court considered that those categories, rather than the date of a reference court’s decision alone, control. The Court regarded the reasoning in Union of India v. Fillip Tiago De Gama of Vedem Vasco De Gama as persuasive on this point, questioned the broader reading in Union of India v. Zora Singh, and distinguished the separate transitional issue addressed in Union of India v. Raghubir Singh.

rule.if: land_acquisition_reference and acquisition_notification_preceded_amendment_effectiveness and collector_award_preceded_transition_trigger and reference_decision_followed_amendment_effectiveness and not (acquisition_pending_without_collector_award_at_trigger or acquisition_commenced_after_trigger)

predicates.land_acquisition_reference: The proceeding is a reference for determination of compensation in a land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_notification_preceded_amendm: The acquisition was initiated under a notification issued before the amendment became effective.
predicates.collector_award_preceded_transition_trig: The Collector made the acquisition award before the transitional trigger specified by the amendment.
predicates.reference_decision_followed_amendment_ef: The court deciding the compensation reference issued its decision after the amendment became effective.
predicates.acquisition_pending_without_collector_aw: The acquisition was pending at the amendment’s transitional trigger and the Collector had not yet made an award.
predicates.acquisition_commenced_after_trigger: The acquisition proceedings commenced after the amendment’s transitional trigger.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition reference has the stated timing and does not fall within either specified transitional category, the claimant is not entitled to the additional acquisition amount under the Court’s view.

issues.legal_issue: Expressly retrospective provisions of an acquisition law extended to a jurisdiction apply to the extent specified even where the acquisition proceedings had previously been governed by a local acquisition law.
material_facts: The local acquisition law had governed acquisition proceedings in the jurisdiction before the central acquisition law was extended there.
The central law was extended to that jurisdiction with effect from the amendment’s commencement.
The amendment expressly gave specified provisions retrospective operation for defined transitional categories.
The State argued that the central law’s provisions could not operate retrospectively on proceedings previously conducted under the local law.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the State’s argument and held that the specified retrospective operation of the central law remained effective for the covered cases, notwithstanding that the central law was extended to the jurisdiction only when the amendment commenced.
issues.legal_principle: The amendment to Section 1(2) extended the principal Act to the jurisdiction, while Section 30 expressly gave certain amended provisions retrospective effect within specified limits. The Court found no inconsistency in giving effect to that express retrospectivity. Relying on Kanthimathy Plantation Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Kerala, it noted that the extension had the same relevant consequences as repeal of the local law, and that Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 applied even though the local law became inoperative through Article 254(1) of the Constitution rather than an express repeal.

predicates.acquisition_proceeding_concerns_prior_lo: The acquisition proceeding arose while a local acquisition regime governed the jurisdiction.
predicates.central_acquisition_law_later_extended_t: A central acquisition law was subsequently extended to the jurisdiction.
predicates.amendment_expressly_prescribes_retroacti: The amendment expressly gives specified provisions retrospective operation.
predicates.acquisition_falls_within_defined_transit: The acquisition falls within a class of cases to which the amendment assigns retrospective operation.

issues.definition: If an acquisition proceeding concerns the prior local regime, the central law is later extended to the jurisdiction, and the acquisition falls within a class expressly covered by retrospective provisions, those specified provisions apply to it.
